title.narrative: Holistic Performance Metrics (ICRAF): Develop and test a guiding framework for designing holistic assessment of food and agricultural systems performance that can be applied across field , farm, household, landscape and food system scales; and position holistic agricultural and food system performance assessments to inform management, planning, policy and investment decisions.

description.narrative: At the outcome level, the Metrics project has delivered a functional demo of the metrics database now available online, alongside a published twopage user brief, with further codesign planned in parallel with stakeholder engagement; a fully developed and openly published metaframework complemented by an emerging practical guidance document; and a substantially advanced evidence base through completion of both holistic and domainspecific metrics reviews, including an innovative AIassisted and manual labelling approach that enabled the screening and labelling of 8,740 articles whose results will feed directly into the database. In addition, the project has contributed to policy dialogue through a peerreviewed publication on measuring agroecology, while laying the groundwork for dedicated policy briefs in the final phase, and has successfully initiated codesign and roadtesting of the metaframework across four projects and multiple contexts in collaboration with ten organisations and initiatives spanning Asia, Africa, Latin America, and global platforms.

title.narrative: Private Sector Incentives and Investments PSii (Bioversity International): Innovative incentives for private sector investments. Improve private and privatepublic sector incentive models to support AE transitions for farmers and consumers. Increase transparency and traceability in supply chains on AE metrics; principles and; enhance capacity of local institutions to engage privatepublic finance models, assessments of policies to support AE transitions

description.narrative: At the outcome level, the Private Sector Incentives and Investments project has strengthened market and institutional engagement through the implementation of five strategic partnerships across three countries, including consolidated MoUs and agreements in Peru, Vietnam, and Ethiopia, with additional partnerships under development. The project has delivered substantial reach and capacity building among producers and valuechain actors, engaging hundreds of farmers and stakeholders through traceability tools, business model and technical trainings, and subsidy support, with notable participation of women and youth, while also scaling training materials in Vietnam to reach up to 10,000 companylinked farmers on lowemission, climatesmart rice production. In parallel, the project is advancing systemic impact by actively developing publicprivate sector policy frameworks in Ethiopia and Peru to support incentives and investments aligned with agroecological and climateresilient transitions.
